subject: Post-demo: Acme Systems — hyperscaler gap observations & A/B test plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmesystems.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmesystems.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Acme Systems — hyperscaler gap observations & A/B test plan

Hi Sara/Tom — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick post-call recap and suggested next steps so we can validate the latency/throughput gaps you saw versus your hyperscaler baseline.

Key observations from our side (summary):
- 95th/99th latency: your sample traces showed ~180ms p95 and ~420ms p99 on the hyperscaler for the 512-token chat workload. Our hosted run (same prompt set, see attached) showed ~140ms p95 / ~260ms p99 — notable p99 improvement but we want to validate under matched concurrency.
- Tokens/sec: at 8 concurrent streams measured ~320 tokens/sec on hyperscaler vs ~420 tokens/sec on Redwood for the same model/quantization profile.
- KV cache behaviour: hyperscaler traces suggest frequent cache misses during multi-turn where our prefix caching should help reduce end-to-end tokens processed.

Proposed A/B plan (short):
1) Shared test harness: we run an A/B against your baseline using your prompt corpus and concurrency profile (we can ingest the same trace file).
2) Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail variability, tokens/sec, throughput (tokens/sec per GPU), and request-level CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Test conditions: identical model version/quantization, same prompt set, cold vs warm cache runs, sustained 30-minute windows to observe microburst behaviour.
4) Ownership & timeline: Redwood to run first pass and share raw CSV; Acme to run a reciprocal job in your hyperscaler account if you want to reproduce.

Attachments: acme_latency_results_v1.csv (our quick-hosted run exported), redwood-ab-test-plan-v1.pdf (draft test protocol).

Ask: can you share the native hyperscaler trace (sample of ~500 requests) and confirm whether we can get a short-lived service account/role to run a 2-hour controlled job in your test subscription? If not, tell us who on your infra team we should coordinate with.

I'll loop Jordan and Marcus for the detailed harness and ops schedule. Proposed week for execution: Aug 26–30.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme Systems — hyperscaler gap observations & A/B test plan

Thanks Connor — good notes. I attached the hyperscaler trace export we discussed (small sample) and a short CSV showing the baseline windows. We'd like the A/B to be as apples-to-apples as possible. A couple of clarifications:

- We run 10 concurrent streams during peak; your note referenced 8 — can you run both 8 and 10?
- We need a non-production credential if you're going to execute inside our account. Can you provide the minimum IAM role permissions you need?
- Timeline: Aug 28–29 would be our preference.

On ownership: we prefer Redwood to run the initial run with our trace (so we can quickly see results) and then give us the scripts to reproduce in our environment. If you can provide a short Mutual Action Plan we'll share with procurement.

Thanks — attaching: acme_hyperscaler_sample_trace.zip, acme_baseline_windows.csv

— Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Product Engineering — Acme Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme Systems — hyperscaler gap observations & A/B test plan

On Wed, 21 Aug 2029 at 09:12, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmesystems.com> wrote:
> Thanks Connor — good notes. I attached the hyperscaler trace export we discussed (small sample) and a short CSV showing the baseline windows.

Quick technical plan and constraints from the ops side:
- Test harness: we'll run a 2-variant A/B in our staging: Redwood runtime (variant A) vs hyperscaler-configured baseline (variant B) using the exact trace + concurrency mix. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and per-request GPU kernel durations.
- Cache states: we should run each variant with (a) cold KV cache (new sessions) and (b) warm KV cache (simulated prior turns) — this is critical since multi-turn cache behaviour explains much of the p99 gap.
- Warmup: 10-minute warmup ramp to reach steady-state before we start measuring the 30-minute capture window.
- Measurement: sample at 1s granularity for tokens/sec and export raw per-request logs plus aggregated CSV.
- Repro: we will provide the harness (locally runnable container + instructions) so Acme can re-run in their account.

IAM perms: we only need a test-role that can create ephemeral VMs/containers and write to a pre-authorized S3/GCS bucket for results. If they can provide a pre-baked service account, even better.

Proposed schedule: Redwood-run in our staging on Aug 28 (variant A & B), share raw results Aug 29 morning PST. If they want reproduction in their account, Acme runs Aug 30.

I'll own the initial run, Marcus will instrument the kernel-level metrics, Marissa will collate the CSVs and visuals for the readout. Connor — can you confirm the mutual action plan for procurement?

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
